findings.body: `test_xfail_world_read_gate_rejects_group_only_rows` is marked `xfail(strict=True)` with a reason stating that group-readable rows must be refused under the offsite posture. The body then asserts `is_federation_memory_publishable(_row(permission_mode=440)) is True` — i.e. that a group-readable (tens digit 4), world-denied row IS publishable. That is the opposite of the stated desired behaviour and of the DEFECT 2 description. If the production gate is ever fixed to read the tens digit, this assertion will fail and the strict xfail will turn into an XPASS-fail, blocking the very fix the test is supposed to signal. The assertion should be `is False` (or removed) to match the documented contract.
findings.title: xfail body contradicts its own desired-behaviour assertion

findings.body: The DEFECT 2 reason and inline comments describe `permission_mode=460` as a 'group-readable, world-denied row' that 'CLEARS the gate purely on its units digit'. But 460 has units digit 0, so `460 % 10 >= 4` is False and the gate refuses it today — the assertion `is False` passes for the wrong reason, and the row is not world-denied (units 0 means no world bit, but the comment's framing of 460 as the offending case is wrong). The actual offending case for the units-digit bug is a mode whose units digit is >= 4 but whose world bit is not set, e.g. 464 (units 4, world bit 4 set — actually world-readable) versus 466/468. A genuinely group-only-but-units>=4 example is 464? No — 464 has world bit 4. The correct example is a mode like 604 (units 4, world bit 4) — again world-readable. The units digit IS the world bit in octal, so `mode % 10 >= 4` is actually a correct world-read test for the units digit; the real defect is that the tens (group) digit is never consulted, so group-readable-but-not-world-readable rows (e.g. 640, 660) are refused rather than the reverse. The reason text and the 460/440 assertions should be rewritten to describe the actual defect (group-readable rows wrongly refused, not wrongly forwarded).
findings.title: 460 is world-readable, not group-only; xfail reason mislabels it

findings.body: In `test_world_read_gate_reads_only_the_world_digit` the comment states '640/660 are world/group-readable under any normal reading of the mode'. 640 and 660 both have units digit 0, i.e. no world-read bit; they are group-readable only. The comment then says they are 'refused only by accident of the units digit' — but refusing them is correct for a world-read gate. The comment conflates the group bit with the world bit and will mislead anyone reading the test as a specification.
findings.title: Comment mischaracterises 640/660 as world-readable

findings.body: `test_xfail_upsert_event_empty_content_is_reported_as_missing` asserts `event['content'] is None` for an empty-content row, but the module's documented default is `''` (the `or ''` fallback), and the companion non-xfail test `test_upsert_event_applies_documented_defaults` explicitly pins `event['content'] == ''`. The two tests encode contradictory expectations for the same input. If the 'defect' is ever 'fixed' to emit None, the non-xfail test breaks; if it is not fixed, the xfail is a permanent strict-xfail that will never XPASS and provides no signal. Either drop the xfail or change the non-xfail test to match.
findings.title: DEFECT 3 xfail asserts a contract the module never promised

findings.body: `test_publish_federation_timeout_is_swallowed` binds `_ = _recorder(...)` and comments that the return value is intentionally unused. The `_recorder` helper already installs the fake as a side effect, so the assignment is dead; the comment is longer than the call. Minor, but the `_ =` idiom plus explanatory comment is noise.
findings.title: Unused recorder binding in timeout test

reviewers.summary: The new characterisation test file is largely well-structured, but several tests encode incorrect expectations about the production behaviour they claim to pin, and one xfail body is internally contradictory. The most serious issue is `test_xfail_world_read_gate_rejects_group_only_rows`: its final assertion (`permission_mode=440` is publishable) contradicts the test's own stated desired behaviour and the DEFECT 2 reason, and the earlier assertion that 460 must be refused is mislabelled as group-only when 460 is in fact world-readable. `test_world_read_gate_reads_only_the_world_digit` also asserts 646 is publishable while its comment claims the units digit alone decides — 646 has units digit 6 so that is consistent, but the comment's claim that 640/660 are 'world/group-readable under any normal reading' is wrong for 640 (units 0 = no world bit). These mischaracterisations will mislead future maintainers and, in the xfail case, will XPASS-fail or silently encode the wrong contract.

findings.body: The test `test_wire_datetime_converts_to_utc_zulu` uses `timezone` and `timedelta` (e.g., `tzinfo=timezone(timedelta(hours=-4))`), but these are not imported in the provided diff. While the instructions state that imports may be in other parts, the `datetime` module itself is imported, but its sub-components `timezone` and `timedelta` are used as if they are in the global namespace, which will cause a `NameError` unless they were explicitly imported as `from datetime import datetime, timezone, timedelta`. Given the context, this is a likely defect in the test setup.
findings.title: Missing imports for datetime components

Chunk 1/7: The first part of the characterisation test suite for `mnemos/persistence/nats_events.py` is well-structured and follows best practices for testing side-effect-heavy modules. It uses monkeypatching and a custom recorder to intercept NATS publishing calls without requiring a live broker. The use of `asyncio.run` within a synchronous wrapper `_run` is a valid way to test coroutines in a synchronous test suite without global async markers.
Chunk 2/7: The reviewed code consists of test cases for NATS event persistence and subject sanitization. The logic for subject segment sanitization, prefixing, and environment-based configuration toggles appears well-covered by the test suite. No defects were identified in this segment.
Chunk 3/7: The reviewed code consists of characterisation tests for NATS event publishing and webhook outbox insertion. The tests cover timeout handling, error propagation, feature flagging, payload construction, and utility functions. No defects were identified in the provided diff.
Chunk 4/7: The test suite contains a logic error in the datetime conversion test due to a missing import of `timezone` and `timedelta` from the `datetime` module.
Chunk 5/7: The diff introduces a comprehensive suite of characterisation tests for `federation_memory_upsert_event` and related logic. The tests cover edge cases including non-mapping row inputs, metadata normalization, datetime stringification, and various fallback behaviors for missing or invalid fields. No defects were identified in the provided code segment.
Chunk 6/7: The test file contains a reference to an undefined `pytest` symbol.
Chunk 7/7: The final part of the test suite adds a characterization test for a known defect regarding empty content strings in federation events. The test is correctly marked as `xfail` with a detailed reason, and it asserts the current (incorrect) behavior to document the existing system state.
